title: Market Surf Report

conditions.headline: Choppy and gray: the lineup waits on Nvidia
conditions.summary: Stock futures are lower for a fourth straight session after Monday's sharp selloff, with the VIX above 23. Nvidia reports after the close and Anthropic's IPO prices Wednesday.

sections.title: Futures & Overnight
items: S&P 500 futures are down about 0.3% and Nasdaq-100 futures about 0.3% in early trading; snapshots varied from -0.1% to -0.4%.
Dow futures are off about 0.4% and Russell 2000 futures about 0.5%.
Monday's session: S&P 500 -1.9%, Nasdaq -2.5% (its worst day since Nov. 5), Dow -1.4%, a third straight loss.
The 10-year Treasury yield eased to about 5.12%; dollar index level was not available in early sources.
WTI crude is near $86 a barrel (+0.3%), gold near $3,860 (+0.2%), bitcoin near $64,300 (-0.2%), and the VIX near 23.5 (+2%).
Asia fell, led by tech after new US curbs on AI chips to China: Nikkei -1.3%, Hang Seng -1.0%, Kospi -2.6%.
Europe opened lower; Deutsche Bank fell about 5% after a Financial Times report on suspicious payments.

sections.title: Macro & Economic Calendar
items: 7:30 AM CT: October retail sales, expected +0.2% m/m (prior +0.8%); ex-autos expected +0.4%.
7:30 AM CT: October import prices, expected +0.7% (prior +1.1%).
8:15 AM CT: October industrial production, expected +0.1% (prior +0.7%).
9:00 AM CT: NAHB homebuilder index, expected 29 (prior 29).
Fed speakers include Waller, Hammack and Williams later today; Musalem is also listed.
CME FedWatch shows about a 97% chance of a quarter-point rate hike in December; FOMC minutes come Wednesday.
Washington tightened China's access to advanced AI chips on Monday, ahead of President Trump's trip to China.

sections.title: Earnings
items: Home Depot reports before the open; consensus is about $3.84 EPS on $42.8 billion in revenue, with focus on DIY spending.
Disney reports before the open; consensus is about $1.69 EPS on $25.2 billion, with focus on streaming profits, parks and the 2027 outlook.
JD.com, Klarna and Elbit Systems are also due this morning; results were not yet out at press time.
After the close: Nvidia, with consensus near $108.9 billion in revenue and $2.47 adjusted EPS; results around 3:20 PM CT, call at 4:00 PM CT.
It is Nvidia's first report since Jensen Huang stepped down as CEO last week; interim CEO Colette Kress leads the call.
ZTO Express and Dolby also report after the close.

sections.title: Stocks in the News
items: NVDA (Nvidia): about -0.4% — earnings tonight; the stock fell 4.1% Monday and is down roughly a quarter this month.
INTC (Intel): -3.3% — Nvidia cut its stake in Intel by 25%.
CRWV (CoreWeave): -2% — AI infrastructure names stay under pressure.
NBIS (Nebius): -0.6% — AI cloud stocks drift lower with Nvidia.
DB (Deutsche Bank): about -5% in Europe — Financial Times report on suspicious payments.
HD (Home Depot) and DIS (Disney): in focus with results due before the bell.
Early pre-market quotes are thin; full mover lists were not available at press time.

sections.title: Business News
items: Anthropic's IPO is set to price Wednesday, with trading expected to begin Thursday.
Nvidia has lost roughly $410 billion in market value since its CEO change, Reuters reports.
New US export curbs on advanced AI chips to China hit Asian chipmakers including Samsung and TSMC.
DoorDash faces Justice Department scrutiny of its $17 billion Instacart deal.
Putin and Xi are set to meet Wednesday, adding to the geopolitical backdrop.

sections.title: What to Watch Today
items: 7:30 AM CT: retail sales and the Home Depot and Disney reactions set the opening tone.
S&P 500 near 7,420 in futures after a three-day slide; watch whether dip buyers show up after the open.
About 3:20 PM CT: Nvidia results, the biggest wave of the week before Anthropic's debut.

script: Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Tuesday, November seventeenth, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Market Surf Report. Riding shotgun on the cabana deck is Gus the wonder dog, nose up and sniffing the sea breeze. Give the Dawn Patrol a good morning, Gus! Alright, let's check the swell. Conditions are poor this morning, gray and choppy. S and P 500 futures are down about three tenths of a percent. Nasdaq one hundred futures are off about three tenths too. Dow futures are down about four tenths, and the Russell two thousand is off about half a percent. These early quotes are thin, so expect some drift. That follows a gnarly Monday. The S and P fell almost two percent, and the Nasdaq dropped two and a half percent, its worst day since early November. The fear gauge, the VIX, is up near twenty three and a half. Now for a bright spot. The ten year Treasury yield slipped about three basis points to around five point one two percent, and gold edged up to around three thousand eight hundred sixty dollars. Gold caught a little wave this morning. That calls for a treat, Gus! Here you go, buddy! Crude is near eighty six dollars, and bitcoin is a touch lower near sixty four thousand. Overseas, Asia wiped out, led by tech after Washington tightened A I chip sales to China. Europe opened lower too. On the wind and weather report, October retail sales land at seven thirty A M Central, with forecasters looking for a gain of two tenths of a percent. Industrial production follows at eight fifteen, and the homebuilder index at nine. Fed speakers Waller, Hammack and Williams are on deck later today, and traders see almost certain odds of a rate hike in December. On the tide chart, Home Depot and Disney report before the bell. The big one is Nvidia after the close, with results around three twenty P M Central. It's the chip Kahuna's first report since its C E O change, and the stock is down roughly a quarter this month. In the lineup, Intel is down about three percent after Nvidia trimmed its stake. CoreWeave is off about two percent. Over in Europe, Deutsche Bank slid about five percent. On beach talk, Anthropic's I P O is set to price Wednesday and start trading Thursday, so the grommet watch is on. Sets to watch today: retail sales at seven thirty, the opening reaction to Home Depot and Disney, and Nvidia this afternoon. Soul surfers, don't drop in on every wave. Got a ticker on your mind? Type any stock, E T F or futures contract into the Check a Wave box on the page, and Surf Daddy will call it for you. This is information, not advice. This is Surf Daddy and Gus the wonder dog saying, if in doubt, paddle out!
